I'm Actually a Goddess
Retour par la Mort
Description : You're actually a goddess of this world. If push comes to shove, you can unleash your hidden divine power. Player characters of any gender can use this cheat.

Merit : Use right after a character in the same Scene performs a check. The check is now counted as a critical. If dice would be added because it is a critical, always add 2d6 regardless of the number of sixes rolled. You can use this once per scenario.
Demerit : Nobody in this world believes you're a goddess. You keep telling them, but everyone either thinnks you must be insane or avoids you out of fear of being damned.
Description : When you died, for reasons related to the world of a deity, you received the ability to come back to life after dying.
Merit : Use when you are knocked out or die. You are no longer knocked out or dead. Your HP becomes 1. You can use this once per scenario.
Demerit : It is not easy to overcome death itself. You need luck on your side. When using Return by Death, you must spend 1 Blessing. If you cannot, then you cannot use Return by Death.
Pursuit of Power
Intoxicated by Pain
Description : You're infatuated with bolstering your magic's power, and you devote yourself wholly to this pursuit.

Merit : Passive. Effective on skills that use dice to determine effects. When you acquire this cheat, choose one spell you already have that deals damage via attack, recovers HP, recovers MP or increases/decreases damage. Add 5d6 to the chosen skill's effects. If you are at least tenth level, add (CL/2)d6 instead.
Demerit : In exchange for power, you pour every last drop of magical energy and life force into your spell. At the end of a process in which you applied the merit's effect, your HP becomes 0.

Description : When you receive physical or mental damage, you feel pleasure instead of pain. You gladly put yourself in harm's way or loose more power than you're capable of for the sake of reveling in that feeling.
Merit : Use right after a damage roll made against you. Change the damage you would receive from that attack to 0. You can use this once per scenario.

Demerit : You are so single-minded in your pursuit of pleasure that your offense suffers, and you neglect to dodge some attacks that come your way. Whenever you make a hit check or dodge check, take a -1d6 penalty.
Belzerg Royalty
Sacred Treasure Holder: Weapon

Description : The blood of the Belzerg royal family, which birthed the legendary hero who slew the Demon Kin, runs through your veins. As such, you've inherited the immense powers of that legendary hero.
Merit : Passive. Add CLx4 to all damage dealth to demon enemies.

Demerit : Your power is propped up by the royal lifestyle you're used to. If you choose stable living or simple living as your Lifestyle, you cannot receive the effects of this cheat's merit, and you take a -1d6 penalty on all checks.

Description : You are the owner of an item said to have been made by the gods in ancient times-- a Sacred Treasure weapon. You know the legeds surrounding your treasure, and what its name is. You can decide for yourself how you came to possess it.
Merit : Item. During Preplay, choose one weapon from your inventory. That weapon becomes a Sacred Treasure. Add CLx3 to its attack power.
Demerit : When you are not equipped with the weapon you chose for this cheat (your Sacred Treasure), you take -2d6 on all checks.
Sacred Treasure Holder: Armor
Member of the Demon King's Army

Description : You are the owner of an item said to have been made by the gods in ancient times-- a Sacred Treasure armor. You know the legeds surrounding your treasure, and what its name is. You can decide for yourself how you came to possess it.
Merit : Item. During Preplay, choose one armor from your inventory. That armor becomes a Sacred Treasure. Add CLx3 to its Physical Defense and CL ot its Magic Defense.
Demerit : When you are not equipped with the armor you chose for this cheat (your Sacred Treasure), you take -2d6 on all checks.

Description : You are part of the Demon King's forces. You've received the Demon King's orders, or permission, to carry out a certain task-- pharps to secretly maintain the barrier around the king's castle. Discuss with the GM what this task should be.
Merit : Passive. Add CLx4 to your Physical Defense and Magic Defense.

Demerit : You cannot refuse a request from the Demon King, nor can you attack any character or enemy who belongs to the Demon King's forces. The GM may set a condition that, when met, enables you to attack such characters or enemies if desired.
Creation Cheat
Destructive Magic Power
Description : You have the ability to create anything you wish. You may decide a reason for this yourself, such as putting knowledge obtained from a goddess to full use.

Merit : You case use this at any time. Create one item with a function of your choosing. Equipment, such as weapons or armor, cannot be obtained with this effect, and you cannot recover Blessings via this merit. The GM has the final decision on the item's final effects. The obtained item vanishes when the scenario ends. You can use this once per scenario.

Demerit : You are tighfisted with money because of what it costs to create things. You refuse to give up on quests and desperately want their rewards. If, for some reason, you cannot gain a quest reward or must give up on it, your number of Blessings immediately becomes 0.

Description : You have obtained magic powers specialized in destruction. The magic attacks you use boast incredible attack power. The player may freely determine the reason they are able to use Destructive Magic Power.
Merit : Use right before a damage roll. Add 10d6 to the damage of a magic attack you perform. If your CL is at least 10, add (CL+2)d6 instead. You can use this once per scenario.
Demerit : You need very precise control over MP in order to use Destructive Magic Power. All spells you use to make magic attacks cost twice the MP.
Villainous Energy
Misunderstood

Description : You're a dead ringer for a villain. A single, wicked lok from you brings misfortune to others like an evil eye. You can freely decide which parts of you are villainous, such as having a villain's face or having an ominous aura about you.
Merit : Use right after a target makes any sort of check. Change the check they performed to a fumble. You can use this once per scenario.
Demerit : People avoid you like the plague. If you buy item's at any time other than character creation, the cost of every item (including Lifestyles) is double for you.

Description : Others think extremely highly of you due to a misunderstanding. As a result, people tend to overly respect your opinions. The player may freely choose what sort of misunderstanding it was.

Merit : Targets all extra characters (or mobs, if in battle) currently in the Scene. Those targets obey your instructions until the end of the Scene, However, whil under this effect, they are treated as extras. You can use this once per scenario.
Demerit : You are awfully conspicuous, and people can't help but pay you a lot of attention. Anyone who makes a hit check for an attack where you are one of the targets gets +1d6 for that hit check.
Loan on Destiny
World of the Strongest

Description : You have received the blessings of fate. Face hardship, and you will coincidentally be saved. The loot you receive on adventures is surprisingly valuable. This is all because you have taken out an advance loan on good luck, diverting you from your original fate.
Merit : Passive. Add 1 to your maximum number of usable Blessings. You can also use Blessings even if it would bring your number of usable Blessings to less than 0.

Demerit : When you are at 0 or less Blessings, all checks you perform, excluding critical rolls, will fail no matter what. Additionally, in After Play, if you Blessings are equal to or less than a negative value of your Luck, you die.
Description : You are the strongest. You have the power to surpass everything anyone could throw at you. There is nobody who can stand in your way.

Merit : Nobody can stand in the way of your supreme might. Use this during the Initiative Process. You immediately perform your Main Process. You can perform this Main Process even when spent, and you don't become spent after it. You can use this once per scenario.

Demerit : Having the mightiest of powers puts a heavy burden on you. After the Main Process from your merit, take -1d6 on every dice roll (such as for checks and damage) you perform until the end of the Scene. This cannot reduce the number of dice you roll to less than 1.
Pursuit Of Skill
Minor Faith
Description : You’ve dedicated your life to improving your performance in a certain skill, you’ve committed everything to mastering that skill.
Merit : Choose a Skill that is not a Spell and requires a dice roll for its effect. Gain +5d6 to its effect. If CL is 10 or more, gain (CL/2)d6 instead.
Demerit : You are literally putting everything on the line, even your life. After using the skill that benefits from this effect, your HP drops to 0.
Description : You worship a god with few followers and monopolise the powers he bestows upon you.

Merit : Write this skill as Minor Faith: (chosen god). Add +2d6 to the Attack Damage, HP recovery, and Damage Reduction effects of (arch)priest skills. If your CL is 10 or more, add + (CL/3)d6 instead.
Demerit : If you acquire a Faith Skill, this cheat will be lost. Also if a character with the same Minor Faith appears in the same scene, the benefits of this cheat cannot be applied.
Super Anxious
Underestimated
Description : You fear failure and want everything to be done with care and perfection, which comes with extensive preparation, lengthy training, and careful research.
Merit : The training and planning you have prepared will come into play. When you reroll a roll due to a Skill or Blessing, add +2d6 to the roll.

Demerit : Before you act, you carefully asses the situation. You must wait on the first round of combat. If you don’t wait, you receive -1d6 on all dice rolls and no benefits until the end of the scene.
Description : Others tend to underestimate your abilities, but once you take action they will see your true abilities.
Merit : Used when you win a Reaction Check. Add +1d6 to your checks and (CL/5+1)d6 to your Attack Damage. This effect lasts until the end of the scenario.
Demerit : While under the effect of this cheat’s benefits, enemies deal an additional (your) CL x 2 damage to you. Enemies may prioritize you or characters they are using to torment you.
Skill Of Mirror
I’d Say I’m Normal
Description : You can perfectly copy the skills you see.

Merit : Can be used at any time. Select one skill used in the scene. You will acquire that skill at the same SL and can use it without class restrictions. In the case of enemy skills, one blessing is consumed. This effect lasts until the end of the scenario.

Demerit : If you have acquired [CL/10 + 1] or more skills through the effect of merit, at the start of the ending phase, you must make a Death Check with difficulty 12. Add -[the number of skills acquried]d6 to this check.
Description : You’re normal. You’ve lived your life turning your back on things like cheats and being a chosen hero.
Merit : Increase your Max HP and Max MP by CL x 3.

Demerit : At the beginning of the Scenario, you are the Cheat. Make a Mind Check with difficulty 8 + CL. If you fail, suffer a fumble. (Note: I have no idea what that fumble would cause, let's the GM decide, take a blessing or keep it for later or something).
Lovely Personality
Guardian Beast
Description : You are the type of person who easily receives the affection of those around you and makes them feel close to you. Whether you like it or not, love and hate are swirling around you.
Merit : Once per Scene. You can ask for one favor within the limits of your abilities. This does not allow you to take any action that would cause HP damage.
Demerit : Your constitution incurs resentment and jealousy. All damage you take is increased by CL x 2.
Description : You have a guardian beast by your side to protect and accompany you. It is very gentle, but can be very scary when angered.
Merit : Once per Scenario, during the Initiative Process, your Guardian Beast can perform a Special Attack. Hit Check 3d6+Mind, Piercing Damage 2d6+10 or CL x 2 for CL 10 or higher.
Demerit : When you are with your Guardian Beast add +1 to the weight of your belongings. If you are not together add -2d6 to all rolls.
Eternal Traveler
Stratège Militaire
Description : Your body does not age, so you have lived a very long life despite your appearance. Those who are standing before you now will one day leave you behind.
Merit : Your body is very resistant to change and you can overcome any bad status. You are immune to negative status effects.
Demerit : You are already becoming an entity that is outside the laws of this world. Gain -1 to your Blessings and Usage Limit. (minimum 1).
Description : You are skilled in military strategy, and it is easy for you to take advantage of situations and turn the tide of battle against overwhelming odds.
Merit : Once per Scenario, Add +10 to the Damage made by any character appearing in the Scene. If CL is 5 or higher add CL x 2 instead. This effect lasts until the end of the scene.
Demerit : Whether it’s preparing your military strategy or your personal life, you are spending a lot of money. Add CL x 100 KE to your Lifestyle cost.
Surpassement des Limites
Description : Whether through talent or hard work, you can hone a skill and just keep on improving it.

Merit : Whenever you acquire a Skill, choose one Skill, it can be one you have not acquired. Its Max SL is increased by 3, CL / 2 if your CL is 10 or higher. It cannot be a Skill whose number of uses or effect does not change with SL.
Demerit : The Max SL for other skills not chosen are 1.
